definition: Gas meter systems measure and record the quantity of gas flowing to a customer or through a process.
example: A utility uses meter readings to calculate monthly consumption.

definition: Gastric bypass surgery alters the digestive tract to reduce stomach capacity and reroute food past part of the small intestine.
example: A bariatric care team monitors nutritional status after gastric bypass.

definition: Gemology is the study and identification of gemstones and their properties.
example: A gemologist distinguishes a natural stone from an imitation by examining its optical properties.

definition: General finance concerns how individuals and organizations raise, allocate and manage money and financial risk.
example: A finance team weighs the cost and timing of funding a new facility.

definition: General sciences encompasses foundational knowledge from several scientific disciplines and their methods.
example: A survey course uses chemistry and biology to explain how pond ecosystems function.

definition: Generative AI uses learned patterns to produce new content such as text, images, audio or code.
example: A designer creates draft layout ideas from a text description.

definition: A geographic coordinate system locates positions on a reference surface using angular coordinates, typically latitude and longitude tied to a datum.
example: A map layer uses geographic coordinates to show wildlife observations across several states.

definition: Geospatial data describes objects or phenomena with information about their location or spatial extent.
example: A file records flood zones as boundary shapes with estimated risk levels.

definition: Geospatial databases store and query data with geographic or geometric properties.
example: A transit planner queries a database for stops within walking distance of a clinic.

definition: Geospatial information technology comprises tools and methods for collecting, managing, analyzing and displaying geographically referenced information.
example: An emergency management team combines satellite imagery, mapping software and field observations to track flooding.

definition: Government finance studies how governments raise revenue, manage debt and budget public spending.
example: A city compares tax revenue and bond proceeds when budgeting a transit extension.

definition: A graph database represents and queries data as entities and relationships, typically expressed as nodes and edges.
example: A travel app finds transfers by following connections among station nodes.

definition: A graphics API defines programming interfaces for using graphics hardware or a rendering system to create images.
example: A game engine submits commands through Vulkan to render its current scene.

definition: A great circle is the intersection of a sphere with a plane passing through its center.
example: A navigator uses a great-circle arc to estimate the shortest surface route between two airports on a spherical Earth model.

definition: The Greeks are sensitivity measures for how an option or derivatives portfolio changes with variables such as underlying price, volatility and time.
example: A risk analyst uses delta to estimate a price change from a small move in the underlying asset.

definition: A green bond is debt issued to finance eligible projects with designated environmental benefits.
example: A city allocates green bond proceeds to an energy-efficient transit project.

definition: The grieving process comprises the varied emotional and practical responses through which people adapt to loss.
example: A bereaved person may alternate between confronting the loss and attending to everyday responsibilities.

definition: A GSM radio access network provides the radio link between GSM mobile devices and the mobile core network.
example: The network coordinates a phone's connection as it moves from one coverage cell to another.

definition: Gynaecology is the medical specialty concerned with the health and disorders of the female reproductive system.
example: A gynaecologist evaluates the cause of persistent pelvic pain.

definition: Hadron physics studies particles made of quarks and gluons and the strong interaction that governs them.
example: Researchers compare measured properties of mesons with predictions about quark interactions.

definition: Health economics and outcomes research examines the costs, effects and patient outcomes of healthcare interventions and systems.
example: A team compares the costs and quality-of-life outcomes of two treatment approaches.

definition: Health, safety and environment is an organizational discipline for managing occupational health, workplace safety and environmental impacts.
example: A manufacturing site reviews worker exposure risks and wastewater controls through its HSE program.

definition: Healthcare delivery science studies how care is organized and provided and how delivery can improve patient outcomes and system performance.
example: A health system compares follow-up scheduling models to reduce missed visits.

definition: Healthcare industry knowledge includes how healthcare providers, insurers, suppliers and regulators interact to deliver and pay for care.
example: A project lead anticipates how insurer reimbursement rules affect a clinic's adoption of a new service.

definition: Healthcare quality concerns how well services increase the likelihood of desired health outcomes and meet accepted standards of care.
example: A hospital tracks preventable readmissions to assess a discharge improvement program.

definition: Higher education law concerns legal rules that govern colleges, universities and their relationships with students, staff and regulators.
example: A university attorney reviews how a disciplinary procedure meets legal obligations.

definition: Higher education policy concerns decisions and rules that shape the goals, funding and operation of colleges and universities.
example: An analyst considers who gains access under a systemwide change to admissions policy.

definition: Hindsight bias is the tendency to see an outcome as more predictable after learning that it occurred.
example: After an outage, a reviewer overestimates how obvious its warning signs were at the time.

definition: Historic preservation is the identification, protection and conservation of buildings, sites and landscapes with historic significance.
example: A preservation team repairs original masonry while adapting a historic building for public use.

definition: Historical linguistics studies how languages change over time and how related languages can be traced to common ancestors.
example: A linguist compares systematic sound correspondences across related languages.

definition: The history of education studies how teaching, schools and access to learning have changed over time.
example: A historian examines who attended newly established public schools and what they were taught.

definition: The history of medicine studies changes in understandings of health, medical practices and healthcare institutions over time.
example: A researcher traces how hospital sanitation practices changed as infection theories developed.

definition: The history of philosophy studies philosophical ideas, arguments and schools in their historical development and context.
example: A seminar compares how ancient and modern philosophers understand the source of moral obligation.

definition: The history of science studies how scientific knowledge and practices develop within changing institutional and cultural contexts.
example: A historian examines how access to new instruments changed what astronomers could measure.

definition: Hockett's design features are proposed properties used to describe human language and compare it with other communication systems.
example: A class uses displacement to discuss how speakers can refer to events that are not present.

definition: Human factors studies how human capabilities and limitations interact with tasks, tools and environments to inform design.
example: A team changes a control panel layout to reduce confusion during time-critical operations.

definition: A human-machine interface is the set of controls and displays through which people exchange information with a machine.
example: A pump operator adjusts the flow setpoint and reads the measured flow on a touchscreen.

definition: The human musculoskeletal system consists of bones, muscles, joints and connective tissues that support the body and enable movement.
example: A therapist explains how the quadriceps and knee joint work together when climbing stairs.

definition: Human rights law concerns legal protections for fundamental rights and freedoms, including the obligations of states to uphold them.
example: A legal researcher compares protections for freedom of expression under national law and international treaties.

definition: HVAC automation systems use sensors, controllers and programmed rules to regulate heating, ventilation and air conditioning.
example: A building controller adjusts airflow based on occupancy and room temperature.
